badl.description: Walk among sharply eroded buttes and colorful sediment layers where ancient horses and rhinos once roamed. Beyond the rock formations, mixed-grass prairie supports bison, bighorn sheep, and prairie dogs.

photo.alt: Layered Badlands ridges rising above patches of prairie after sunset.

bibe.description: Follow the Rio Grande into limestone canyons, then look toward the Chisos Mountains rising out of the Chihuahuan Desert. Big Bend pairs expansive desert hikes and mountain views with the dark skies of far West Texas.

photo.alt: Sunset beyond the Window, framed by the Chisos Mountains.

bisc.description: Trade the highway for mangrove shorelines, island waters, and coral reefs at the northern end of the Florida Keys. Explore Biscayne by boat or paddle its shallow bay, with underwater landscapes adding another dimension to the visit.

photo.alt: Twilight at Boca Chita in Biscayne National Park.
photo.credit: National Park Service Digital Image Archives

blca.description: Peer into a narrow gorge where the Gunnison River cuts between sheer cliffs and jagged rock spires. Rim trails and overlooks reveal a dramatic vertical landscape, with the river far below and ancient rock rising around it.

photo.alt: Backlit cliffs of Black Canyon of the Gunnison at sunset.

brca.description: Look out across amphitheaters crowded with orange, pink, and pale stone hoodoos, then descend between the spires for a different perspective. Bryce Canyon's high plateau combines sweeping rim views with trails that bring its intricate rock formations close.

photo.alt: Stone hoodoos in Bryce Canyon National Park.

cany.description: Stand above a maze of canyons and mesas shaped by the Colorado and Green rivers, or explore trails among the striped sandstone spires of the Needles. Canyonlands opens onto immense desert views, with each district offering a different way into the landscape.

photo.alt: Mesa Arch standing at the top of a high sandstone cliff in Canyonlands.

care.description: Explore cliffs, natural bridges, and folded bands of colorful rock along the Waterpocket Fold. Around Fruita, historic farms and orchards sit beneath sandstone walls, bringing a human scale to Capitol Reef's sweeping desert geology.

photo.alt: The Castle's red sandstone cliffs above tree-lined Sulphur Creek.

cave.description: Step beneath the Chihuahuan Desert into vast limestone chambers filled with sculpted cave formations. Carlsbad Caverns contrasts the underground scale of the Big Room with rocky canyons and desert life above the surface.

photo.alt: Historic black-and-white photograph of formations near the Temple of the Sun in Carlsbad Cavern's Big Room.

chis.description: Leave the mainland behind for five islands shaped by sea cliffs, isolation, and the Pacific Ocean. Coastal walks and boat journeys reveal a Southern California landscape with distinctive plants and animals found nowhere else.

photo.alt: A boat approaching Painted Cave on Santa Cruz Island.

chir.description: Wind through a landscape of rhyolite pinnacles, balancing rocks, and shaded passages carved from ancient volcanic deposits. Scenic drives and hiking trails bring Chiricahua's standing rocks into view from both the overlooks and the spaces between them.

photo.alt: Pinnacles and balancing rocks at Chiricahua.

cong.description: Step beneath towering old-growth trees into a floodplain forest nourished by the Congaree and Wateree rivers. Cypress knees, broad-bottomed trunks, and the wooded waters of Cedar Creek make Congaree an invitation to look slowly and explore at forest level.

photo.alt: Trees lining the still waters of Cedar Creek at Congaree.

crla.description: Look down into intensely blue water held inside the collapsed summit of an ancient volcano. Crater Lake's rim viewpoints and mountain scenery reveal the scale of an eruption that reshaped this Cascade peak about 7,700 years ago.

photo.alt: Panoramic winter view of Crater Lake and the Watchman lookout.

cuva.description: Follow the winding Cuyahoga River through forests, rolling hills, and open farmland between Cleveland and Akron. Walk or cycle the Towpath Trail to trace the Ohio & Erie Canal through a landscape where nature and transportation history meet.

photo.alt: Brandywine Falls flowing over layered rock in Cuyahoga Valley.

deva.description: Explore a below-sea-level desert basin framed by mountains, sculpted dunes, and deeply cut canyons. Death Valley's stark landscapes reward a closer look, from the shapes of the Mesquite Dunes to natural rock bridges and small oases.

photo.alt: Weathered mesquite wood exposed among the Mesquite Flat Sand Dunes.

drto.description: Cross open water to a cluster of small islands where Fort Jefferson rises above blue sea and coral reefs. Dry Tortugas combines a remote island journey with coastal history, bird habitat, and an underwater world reached by boat or seaplane.

photo.alt: Aerial view of Fort Jefferson and the surrounding sea in 1993.

ever.description: Explore a vast South Florida landscape where wetlands, forests, and coastal waters form connected habitats for native wildlife. From trails to paddling waters, Everglades invites you into the meeting places of marsh and mangrove.

photo.alt: Water lilies beside the elevated Anhinga Trail boardwalk in Everglades.

jeff.description: Stand beneath the Gateway Arch on the Mississippi riverfront and explore the city's role in the nation's westward expansion. The park also preserves the story of Dred and Harriet Scott, who sued for their freedom in the Old Courthouse.

photo.alt: The Gateway Arch beside trees and the downtown St. Louis skyline.

glac.description: Travel through glacier-carved valleys, alpine meadows, and mountain lakes along Going-to-the-Sun Road. With more than 700 miles of trails, Glacier offers both sweeping roadside views and paths deeper into its rugged mountain landscape.

photo.alt: Lake McDonald beneath cloud-covered mountains on an autumn day.

grca.description: Look across a mile-deep canyon where the Colorado River has exposed a vast landscape of layered rock. From the rim, changing viewpoints reveal side canyons, distant cliffs, and the immense scale of the river's work.

photo.alt: Visitors looking across Grand Canyon from Ooh Aah Point on South Kaibab Trail.

grte.description: Watch the Teton skyline rise above lakes and the broad valley of Jackson Hole. Explore a landscape where alpine scenery, wildlife habitat, and generations of human history share the same mountain backdrop.

photo.alt: The Teton Range in autumn.

grba.description: Climb from sagebrush foothills toward Wheeler Peak and walk among ancient bristlecone pines. Great Basin brings high-mountain scenery, underground passages, and dark night skies together in a remote corner of Nevada.

photo.alt: Great Basin National Park viewed from Lexington Road.

grsa.description: Climb sweeping sand ridges with the Sangre de Cristo Mountains rising behind them. Beyond the dunes, Great Sand Dunes protects grasslands, wetlands, forests, alpine lakes, and tundra, making this far more than a desert scene.

photo.alt: Visitors on sand dunes below the snow-capped Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

grsm.description: Follow wooded mountain ridges and streams through a landscape rich in Appalachian plant life and history. Historic homes, barns, churches, and gristmills add stories of mountain communities to the Great Smokies' forest scenery.

photo.alt: A road winding through the Great Smoky Mountains.

gumo.description: Hike into mountains and canyons built from an ancient Permian reef, with desert country stretching below the heights. Guadalupe Mountains protects Texas's four highest peaks alongside dunes, diverse habitats, and stories of people who made lives in this rugged borderland.

photo.alt: The Guadalupe Mountains rising above desert terrain.

hosp.description: Walk from grand historic bathhouses into forested hills above a city built around thermal springs. Hot Springs brings together bathing culture, mountain views, and the geology of naturally heated water in the heart of town.

photo.alt: The Hale Bathhouse's stucco facade, red tile roof, and rounded windows.

indu.description: Follow Lake Michigan's shore from sandy beaches and wind-shaped dunes into woods, prairies, and wetlands. Indiana Dunes packs striking habitat variety into 15 miles of lakeshore, with more than 50 miles of trails to explore beyond the beach.

photo.alt: Central Beach on the Lake Michigan shore at Indiana Dunes.

isro.description: Cross Lake Superior to a rugged island wilderness of rocky shores and secluded hiking routes. Isle Royale offers a chance to travel at the pace of a backpack, paddle, or boat, far from the mainland road network.

photo.alt: Aerial view of Ojibway Fire Tower above Isle Royale's wooded landscape.

jotr.description: Explore the meeting place of the Mojave and Colorado deserts, where distinctive plants and sculpted rock formations give the landscape its character. Joshua Tree combines desert walking, unusual geology, and dark night skies in a wide-open Southern California setting.

photo.alt: Joshua trees in a foggy desert landscape.
photo.credit: Joshua Tree National Park / NPS Photo

kica.description: Walk among giant sequoias, then look toward the rugged mountains and deep canyons of the Sierra Nevada. Kings Canyon combines the immense trees of Grant Grove with a landscape that opens into far larger mountain wilderness.

photo.alt: Historic view of the South Fork Kings River near Zumwalt Meadow, photographed in 1981.

lavo.description: Explore a volcanic landscape where jagged peaks rise above mountain lakes and meadows, and hot water still reshapes the ground. Lassen Volcanic pairs the scenery of an alpine park with fumaroles and other evidence of heat beneath the surface.

photo.alt: A park road lined with tall pine trees in Lassen Volcanic.

maca.description: Step into the world's longest known cave system, where underground passages add another dimension to Kentucky's rolling hills. Above ground, river valleys and wooded backcountry reveal a different side of Mammoth Cave's landscape.

photo.alt: Stairs descending from the forest into Mammoth Cave's Historic Entrance.

meve.description: Look into cliff alcoves and across mesas where Ancestral Pueblo communities built their homes over more than 700 years. Mesa Verde offers a close encounter with enduring architecture and a living cultural heritage connected to 27 Pueblos and Tribes.

photo.alt: Cliff Palace's stone buildings sheltered beneath a rock alcove at Mesa Verde.

mora.description: Follow forested slopes toward the glacier-covered summit of Mount Rainier, an active volcano rising above Washington's landscape. Mountain trails, subalpine meadows, and cascading water reveal different sides of a peak that feeds five major rivers.

photo.alt: Mount Rainier's glaciated summit above a rocky ridge and conifer trees.

neri.description: Look across a deep gorge carved by a rugged north-flowing river, then explore trails, overlooks, and the stories of river communities. New River Gorge brings whitewater and wooded canyon scenery together beneath its sweeping steel bridge.

photo.alt: The New River Gorge Bridge spanning the river and wooded gorge.

noca.description: Explore jagged peaks, glacier-shaped heights, and forested valleys threaded with cascading water. North Cascades offers mountain trails and wild backcountry where dramatic elevation changes bring very different landscapes close together.

photo.alt: Castle Rock summit with a backdrop of snow-capped North Cascades peaks.
photo.credit: Courtesy of North Cascades National Park Service Complex; NPS Staff

olym.description: Move between glacier-capped mountains, old-growth temperate rain forest, and a wild Pacific coastline. Olympic's nearly million-acre landscape invites very different journeys, from high-country views to forest walks and rocky shores.

photo.alt: A lake at Olympic surrounded by forest and mountain slopes.

pefo.description: Walk through colorful badlands and past ancient logs transformed into brilliantly patterned stone. Petrified Forest connects more than 200 million years of geologic history with ancestral Puebloan sites and traces of historic Route 66.

photo.alt: Petrified wood at Petrified Forest National Park.

pinn.description: Hike among volcanic rock spires, oak woodlands, and shaded canyons, with talus caves adding a hidden dimension to the terrain. Pinnacles pairs unusual geology with habitat protected for California condors.

photo.alt: Sunset light on Pinnacles' rocky High Peaks beneath a purple sky.

redw.description: Walk beneath towering coast redwoods, then explore a landscape that reaches into prairies, rivers, and the Pacific shore. Redwood's forest groves are only part of a much larger coastal world shaped by both ancient ecosystems and enduring human connections.

photo.alt: Fog among the trunks of an ancient coast redwood forest.

romo.description: Follow mountain trails from open meadows and subalpine forest toward lakes and the rocky heights of the alpine tundra. Rocky Mountain offers a landscape of changing elevations, where each climb reveals a different view of Colorado's high country.

photo.alt: Lake Helene beneath snowy peaks along the Continental Divide.

sagu.description: Walk among giant saguaros rising above the Sonoran Desert, with the cactus landscape stretching across two districts on opposite sides of Tucson. Saguaro offers a close look at the plants and wildlife adapted to this distinctive corner of the American Southwest.

photo.alt: A tall branching saguaro above prickly pear and paloverde vegetation.

sequ.description: Walk beneath giant sequoias and look upward into the rugged mountain country of the Sierra Nevada. Sequoia combines immense living trees with foothills, deep canyons, and high-country wilderness on a scale that reaches far beyond the forest groves.

photo.alt: Visitors gathered beside the enormous trunk of the General Sherman Tree.

shen.description: Follow the Blue Ridge through wooded hollows, waterfall country, and overlooks facing layers of mountain scenery. Shenandoah's forests shelter deer, songbirds, and black bears, while its trails invite a closer look beyond the drive.

photo.alt: Lands Run Falls cascading through green woodland at Shenandoah.

thro.description: Explore striped badland buttes and the winding Little Missouri River in the country that helped shape Theodore Roosevelt's conservation outlook. Scenic views and trails connect the rugged landscape with the story of his years in Dakota Territory.

photo.alt: Sunlight breaking through clouds over badland buttes and the Little Missouri River.

voya.description: Travel into a northern Minnesota landscape of broad lakes, forested shores, and ancient granite rising from the water. Voyageurs carries the memory of French-Canadian canoe travelers into a park where exploring by water remains central to the experience.

photo.alt: Rock formations and water in Voyageurs National Park.
photo.credit: National Park Service Digital Image Archives

whsa.description: Walk into wave-like dunes of white gypsum, where wind draws ripples and sharp ridgelines across the Tularosa Basin. White Sands protects part of an enormous dunefield and the plants and animals that have adapted to life among its shifting sands.

photo.alt: Visitors walking down gypsum dunes during a White Sands sunset program.

wica.description: Explore two contrasting worlds: a complex cave below ground and rolling prairie and forested hills above it. Wind Cave's delicate calcite boxwork shares the park with grassland habitat for bison, elk, and other wildlife.

photo.alt: A bison bull standing in frosty prairie grass at Wind Cave.

yell.description: Explore a landscape where geysers and brilliantly colored hot springs reveal heat close beneath the surface. Yellowstone pairs these hydrothermal wonders with wild country that supports bison, wolves, bears, and elk.

photo.alt: Visitors on the Midway Geyser Basin boardwalk beneath a wide plume of steam.

yose.description: Look up at immense granite walls, explore waterfall country, and follow the landscape from deep valleys toward High Sierra meadows. Yosemite brings giant sequoias, glacier-shaped scenery, and mountain wilderness together far beyond its famous valley.

photo.alt: Yosemite Valley's granite cliffs seen from Tunnel View.
photo.credit: U. S. National Park Service (publisher; photographer unknown)

zion.description: Walk into a canyon of towering sandstone walls, where cream, pink, and red cliffs rise above the river corridor. From broad views near the Watchman to the close walls of the Narrows, Zion offers striking changes in scale as you explore.

photo.alt: The Watchman rising above the river corridor at the mouth of Zion Canyon.

dena.description: Follow a single park road from taiga forest toward open tundra and the great Alaska Range. Denali's six-million-acre landscape is habitat for wide-ranging wildlife, with North America's tallest peak rising beyond the lower valleys.

photo.alt: North America's tallest mountain appearing between clouds above Eielson Bluffs.

gaar.description: Enter a roadless Arctic landscape of glacier-carved valleys, wild rivers, and mountain passes. Gates of the Arctic offers wilderness travel without established park trails, in country where people have lived with the land for more than ten thousand years.

photo.alt: A rainbow over the Arctic Divide in Gates of the Arctic.

glba.description: Travel into sheltered fjords surrounded by glaciers, rugged mountains, and temperate rain forest. Glacier Bay is both a dramatic coastal wilderness and the homeland of Huna and Yakutat Lingit people, with stories that reach from the shoreline to the ice.

photo.alt: Margerie Glacier extending from the mountains toward Glacier Bay in 2010.

katm.description: Explore salmon waters and brown-bear habitat in a landscape transformed by the 1912 Novarupta eruption. From Brooks Falls to the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes, Katmai brings living ecosystems and stark volcanic history into the same journey.

photo.alt: Katmai Caldera and glacier with Mount Griggs in the distance.

kefj.description: Explore a coast of steep fjords and forests beneath glaciers flowing from the Harding Icefield. Kenai Fjords offers very different perspectives from the Exit Glacier trails and the waters along its ice-carved shoreline.

photo.alt: Aerial view of Aialik Glacier descending from the Harding Icefield.

kova.description: Discover Arctic sand dunes, mountain scenery, and the winding Kobuk River in a landscape crossed by generations of people and caribou. Kobuk Valley links an unexpected dunefield with the continuing cultural traditions of Onion Portage.

photo.alt: Two researchers crossing the sand dunes of Kobuk Valley.

lacl.description: Explore turquoise lakes, craggy mountains, and glacier-shaped country in a landscape still closely tied to local life. Lake Clark connects wilderness scenery with salmon habitat, volcanic geology, and the waterside community of Port Alsworth.

photo.alt: A biologist collecting a water sample from a boat on a lake in Lake Clark National Park.

wrst.description: Look toward immense mountains and glaciers in a park that rises from the coast to peaks above 18,000 feet. Wrangell-St. Elias offers room for ambitious wilderness journeys across 13.2 million acres, alongside the continuing lives of people connected to the land.

photo.alt: Sunrise over the Wrangell Mountains viewed from Willow Lake.

hale.description: Explore stark volcanic slopes and colorful cinder landscapes high above Maui's coast. Haleakala also protects a separate world of subtropical rain forest, with Hawaiian cultural connections linking the mountain and its living ecosystems.

photo.alt: Sliding Sands Trail crossing the open floor of Haleakala's volcanic crater.

havo.description: Explore the landscapes of Kilauea and Mauna Loa, where volcanic summits, lava formations, and rain forest tell different chapters of an island's growth. Hawaii Volcanoes connects powerful geology with ecosystems and cultural places held sacred for centuries.

photo.alt: Lava erupting from vents in Halemaumau crater during the June 2023 eruption.

npsa.description: Explore volcanic islands where tropical rain forest reaches toward the coast and coral reefs add another world offshore. The National Park of American Samoa brings South Pacific landscapes together with the living Samoan culture that gives these places meaning.

photo.alt: Ofu's sandy beach and fringing reef with Olosega rising in the distance.

viis.description: Go beyond St. John's white-sand beaches to coral reefs, Indigenous petroglyphs, and historic plantation sites. Virgin Islands pairs island scenery with a history that includes Taino communities and the enslaved people whose labor sustained the sugar economy.

photo.alt: Panoramic view of Trunk Bay's beach, wooded shore, and turquoise water on St. John.

acad.description: Follow granite ridgelines above the Atlantic, wander forest trails beside freshwater lakes, and watch waves break against the rocky Maine coast. Acadia brings mountain hikes, historic carriage roads, and ocean scenery together in one compact coastal landscape.

photo.alt: Waves breaking against granite ledges at Schoodic Point in Acadia.

arch.description: Walk beneath sweeping sandstone arches and between towering rock fins in Utah's red-rock desert. From roadside overlooks to the hike toward Delicate Arch, exploring Arches reveals how dramatically stone can frame the open sky.

photo.alt: Delicate Arch above a sandstone basin with distant ridges and mountains.

amis.description: Follow desert shores and open water along the United States portion of Amistad Reservoir. Paddling, hiking, and cultural traces reaching back nearly 5,000 years bring the borderland's natural and human stories together.

photo.alt: Sunset over Amistad Reservoir with Highway 90 bridge to left of photo going over the reservoir and i

bica.description: Explore a canyon landscape spread across more than 120,000 acres, with lake waters, rugged overlooks, and historic ranches. Bighorn sheep habitat and more than 10,000 years of human history add depth to the scenery.

photo.alt: Summer view of the Yellowtail Dam from the Ok-A-Beh road.

boha.description: Leave the city shore for a network of 34 harbor islands and peninsulas. Explore tide pools, island trails, historic lighthouses, and Civil War-era Fort Warren with Boston's skyline across the water.

photo.alt: A child dancing on the beach at dusk

chat.description: Follow wooded riverbanks past rocky shoals and the stone remains of old mills. The Chattahoochee offers paddling, fishing, and walking through a river corridor that also supports nesting great blue herons.

photo.alt: Two adult Great Blue Herons stand watch over their 3 young chicks in the nest.

chic.description: Follow spring-fed creeks beneath historic bridges, or head onto the broad waters of Lake of the Arbuckles. Chickasaw brings freshwater springs, lakeside recreation, and a resident bison herd into one varied landscape.

photo.alt: Lincoln Bridge with Travertine Creek flowing below

cure.description: Explore three reservoirs framed by mesas, rock pinnacles, and steep canyon walls. Curecanti pairs boating and shoreline walks with a changing landscape of sagebrush country and forest.

photo.alt: A single boat floating out in a reservoir. Mesas surrounding the area are reflected on the water.

dewa.description: Follow 40 miles of the Delaware River through a long corridor of wooded ridges, waterfalls, and historic places. Trails and paddling routes reveal both the river's mountain gap and quieter stretches of valley.

photo.alt: View of the Delaware River cutting between two low mountain peaks

gate.description: Explore beaches, salt marshes, and historic coastal structures across 27,000 acres around New York Harbor. Gateway links urban shorelines with bird habitat at Jamaica Bay and the lighthouse landscape of Sandy Hook.

photo.alt: Red pink and orange sky over a body of water

gari.description: Take on the Gauley's steep-sided gorge, where 25 miles of river and six miles of the Meadow River wind through wooded valleys. Powerful rapids make this a destination for experienced whitewater trips.

photo.alt: Rafters enjoying the Gauley River

glca.description: Explore more than 1.25 million acres of desert canyons, sandstone walls, and Lake Powell shoreline. Scenic overlooks and backcountry routes reveal a landscape stretching from Lees Ferry into southern Utah.

photo.alt: Woman raises her arms while standing in front of a sandstone butte

goga.description: Walk from bayfront beaches to windswept headlands and former military posts around the Golden Gate. Nineteen ecosystems support more than 2,000 plant and animal species across this varied coastal park.

photo.alt: White buildings with red roofs at Crissy Field with blue bay and Golden Gate Bridge and fog behind.

lach.description: Arrive at the head of Lake Chelan to find mountain trails, forested valleys, and the small community of Stehekin. This lake-accessed corner of the North Cascades pairs deep-water scenery with a quieter mountain approach.

photo.alt: boats on the water with mountains and trees surrounding

lake.description: Explore 1.5 million acres of desert mountains, canyons, and the broad waters of lakes Mead and Mohave. Paddle beneath Black Canyon's walls or follow land routes into the Mojave landscape.

photo.alt: sun rising on Black Canyon
photo.credit: NPS Photo/Andrew Cattoir 【4†Image: picnic area at Redstone】 There are many picnic areas at Lake Mead NRA

lamr.description: Drop below the Texas plains into colorful, 200-foot canyon breaks carved by the Canadian River. Lake Meredith's coves and shoreline trails reveal seven habitats within this rugged grassland setting.

photo.alt: A boat travels across Lake Meredith on a sunny day. The lake is light blue.

laro.description: Follow the Columbia River reservoir through stone-walled country shaped by Ice Age floods. Shoreline stops connect boating and walking with stories of Indigenous communities, traders, settlers, and the building of Grand Coulee Dam.

photo.alt: Various motorboats on a blue lake, landscaped by tall tree filled hills.

rola.description: Follow the North Cascades Highway past forested slopes and the blue-green waters of Diablo and Ross lakes. Trails and lakeside camps lead deeper into a mountain corridor shaped by rivers, glaciers, and hydropower.

photo.alt: boats on the water with mountains and trees surrounding

samo.description: Explore chaparral-covered ridges, coastal canyons, and Malibu beaches along a network of more than 500 miles of trails. Native American cultural sites and former movie ranches add human stories to the mountain scenery.

photo.alt: Sunbeams reaching from glowing sun over the ocean.
photo.credit: NPS 【4†Image: Trail view with yellow flowers in the foreground that lead to green mountains against a blue sky.】 Zuma Canyon in spring.

whis.description: Explore 42,000 acres around Whiskeytown Lake, with waterfalls, rugged trails, and Gold Rush-era buildings. Forests recovering from fire reveal another chapter in this northern California landscape.

photo.alt: Blue-gray waters of lake with green shrub in foreground, mountains and clouds in background.

biso.description: Explore 125,000 acres of the Cumberland Plateau, where sandstone bluffs and wooded gorges frame a free-flowing river. Trails, overlooks, and river routes reveal the Big South Fork's rugged terrain.

photo.alt: Big South Fork NRRA in Fall

miss.description: Follow a 72-mile reach of the Mississippi through the Twin Cities, from urban riverfronts to quieter islands and wooded banks. Walking, cycling, and paddling routes connect river scenery with the history of communities along its shores.

photo.alt: Large canoes and crews paddle down the river amidst autumnal color.

arpo.description: Explore a riverside meeting place where cultures traded, settled, and competed for control of the lower Mississippi region. Trails through the former post's landscape connect its layered human history with river scenery.

photo.alt: confluence of two rivers

arho.description: Look across the Potomac from the hilltop home associated with Robert E. Lee and the Custis family. The house and grounds open difficult questions about slavery, military service, and the Civil War.

photo.alt: Columns of Arlington House

cham.description: Walk the borderland grounds that commemorate the peaceful settlement of a century-long dispute between Mexico and the United States. The memorial connects diplomacy with the cultures of the Rio Grande region.

photo.alt: a bench next to a tree with U.S. and Mexican flags flying against a mountain background

coro.description: Explore rugged borderland mountains while considering the consequences of Coronado's expedition and its encounters with Indigenous peoples. Desert views give scale to a story of conquest, cultural exchange, and lasting change.

photo.alt: Agave stalks and wildflowers with mountains in the distance

deso.description: Follow the coastal landscape associated with Hernando de Soto's 1539 landing in Tampa Bay. The memorial examines the expedition's search for wealth and the Indigenous resistance to an invasion of their homelands.

photo.alt: Reenactor Bill Boston on his horse Dixie in front of the De Soto Monument.

ddem.description: Encounter the story of Dwight D. Eisenhower through an outdoor memorial in the nation's capital. Its sculptures and expansive setting invite a closer look at his military leadership and presidency.

photo.alt: Dwight D. Eisenhower Memorial Entrance

feha.description: Stand at the Wall Street site where George Washington took his first presidential oath in 1789. The present memorial connects this small stretch of Manhattan with the first Congress and the beginnings of the federal government.

photo.alt: “Large crowd inside the rotunda of Federal Hall National Memorial”

flni.description: Walk a landscape of remembrance honoring Flight 93's 40 passengers and crew, who resisted their hijackers on September 11, 2001. The memorial brings their individual lives and collective actions into focus.

photo.alt: Field of white and yellow wildflowers with a white wall in the distance and blue sky above.

foca.description: Explore the riverfront setting of a short-lived French settlement in sixteenth-century Florida. Fort Caroline's story connects European rivalry with the lives and homelands of the Timucua people.

photo.alt: Living history volunteers portraying French soldiers at Fort Caroline
photo.credit: Courtesy of the National Park Service

frde.description: Follow a sequence of outdoor memorial spaces beside the Tidal Basin, with sculpture and water recalling Franklin D. Roosevelt's presidency. The setting invites reflection on the Depression, war, and his enduring political legacy.

photo.alt: Picture of FDR in a wheel chair within his memorial

gegr.description: Step into the monumental tomb of Ulysses S. Grant and his wife, Julia, above the Hudson River. The mausoleum connects the Union commander's Civil War service with his presidency and the unfinished work of Reconstruction.

photo.alt: Mausoleum and flags in sunny weather

hagr.description: Visit the country home Alexander Hamilton built in what is now Harlem. Its early American architecture offers a personal entry into the life of a Revolutionary soldier and the first secretary of the Treasury.

photo.alt: Hamilton Grange National Memorial

jofl.description: Look across the remains of South Fork Dam, whose failure unleashed the devastating Johnstown flood of May 31, 1889. The landscape makes the disaster's scale tangible and explores the human decisions behind it.

photo.alt: A farmhouse, shed, and long, red barn with windows atop a grassy hill

kowa.description: Walk beside sculpted servicemen and a reflective wall honoring those who served in the Korean War. The memorial's faces and figures bring an often distant conflict into a personal setting.

photo.alt: Dawn Picture of the statues within the memorial
photo.credit: NPS Photo/Carol Highsmith 【4†Image: The American flag is centered in the backgrounds between two walkways.】 Korean War Veterans Memorial in the summer

libo.description: Explore the southern Indiana landscape where Abraham Lincoln grew up. A recreated pioneer farm and memorial grounds connect everyday frontier work with the formative years of the future president.

photo.alt: Cabin and smokehouse in the fall

linc.description: Climb the broad steps to Lincoln's seated marble figure, with the Reflecting Pool stretching toward the Washington Monument. The memorial brings his words on union and freedom into a setting that also became central to the civil rights movement.

photo.alt: Lincoln Memorial at Dusk

lyba.description: Follow winding paths through white pines and an open meadow overlooking Washington across the Potomac. Chosen by Lady Bird Johnson, this grove honors Lyndon Johnson's legacy in social justice and conservation.

photo.alt: The Memorial

mlkm.description: Encounter Martin Luther King Jr.'s stone likeness beside the Tidal Basin. The memorial pairs a striking sculptural setting with words from his struggle for racial equality, freedom, and justice.

photo.alt: Statue of Martin Luther King, Jr.

moru.description: Look up at the immense faces of Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt, and Lincoln carved into the Black Hills granite. The memorial offers a place to examine the presidents' legacies alongside the region's longer Indigenous history.

photo.alt: Photo of Mount Rushmore under a bright blue sky with puffy clouds floating over.

pevi.description: See a 352-foot Doric column rise above Lake Erie, commemorating the War of 1812's Battle of Lake Erie. The island memorial also celebrates the lasting peace among the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

photo.alt: 9-3'x5' international flags line sidewalk that leads to a white building with green roof. Tall stone

poch.description: Remember the 320 men killed when ammunition ships exploded at Port Chicago on July 17, 1944. The memorial connects this wartime disaster with segregation and the struggle for racial equality in the military; access requires advance arrangements.

photo.alt: Port Chicago Memorial

rowi.description: Explore the place where Roger Williams founded Providence in 1636 after banishment from Massachusetts. The memorial grounds introduce his defense of religious liberty and the Indigenous relationships that made the settlement possible.

photo.alt: View of the historic well through crabapple trees

thko.description: Visit the modest Philadelphia house where Polish military engineer Thaddeus Kosciuszko recovered from his wounds. His story links Revolutionary War fortifications with a wider struggle for liberty and human rights.

photo.alt: Color photo showing a three story brick rowhouse on a corner lot.

this.description: Cross to a Potomac island of wooded uplands and marshy lowlands, reshaped in the 1930s as a living memorial to Theodore Roosevelt. Forest paths place his conservation legacy within sight of the capital.

photo.alt: A bronze statue of Theodore Roosevelt standing and pointing.

jefm.description: Approach the columned memorial to Thomas Jefferson across the Tidal Basin landscape. Inside, his statue and selected writings invite reflection on the Declaration of Independence and the contradictions of his life.

photo.alt: Thomas Jefferson Memorial reflects on Tidal Basin
photo.credit: Library of Congress/Carol Highsmith 【4†Image: The Thomas Jefferson Memorial with flowering trees in the foreground】 The Thomas Jefferson Memorial framed by cherry blossoms

vive.description: Follow the dark, reflective wall bearing the names of Americans who died or remain missing from the Vietnam War. The descending path creates an intimate space for remembrance within the National Mall.

photo.alt: Lights glow at the base of the wall of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial with Washington Monument.

wamo.description: Look up the 555-foot marble obelisk built to honor George Washington. Its unmistakable silhouette anchors the National Mall and frames views across the capital's memorial landscape.

photo.alt: Washington Monument at Dusk

wwim.description: Pause in the capital's memorial landscape to remember the 4.7 million Americans who served in World War I. Sculpture and commemorative spaces connect individual sacrifice with a war that reshaped the twentieth century.

photo.alt: General Pershing Statue
photo.credit: NPS Photo 【4†Image: An elevated platform overlooks the World War I Memorial】 The Belvedere is the conceptual center of the World War I Memorial, providing a commanding view of its major features.

wwii.description: Walk between stone pillars, bronze details, and fountains honoring Americans who served during World War II. The gold-star wall gives a solemn focus to the memorial's broad ceremonial setting.

photo.alt: Close up of Gold Stars in the Memorial

wrbr.description: Stand near the sandy ground where Wilbur and Orville Wright achieved powered airplane flight on December 17, 1903. Flight markers and the hilltop memorial turn a familiar invention story into a landscape you can walk.

photo.alt: Orville takes to the air in the flyer for the first time as Wilbur assists.
photo.credit: Wilbur Wright, Orville Wright, and John Daniels

blri.description: Follow a 469-mile mountain road through the Appalachian Highlands, with overlooks opening onto layered ridges and pastoral valleys. Short walks and roadside stops reveal the landscape at a slower pace.

photo.alt: A long pine tree stands in front of distant mountain ridges beneath an orange sunset

natr.description: Trace a 444-mile scenic road through Mississippi, Alabama, and Tennessee. Stops along the way connect forest and field with the older travel corridor used by Indigenous peoples, traders, settlers, and soldiers.

photo.alt: A slightly curvy section of the Natchez Trace Parkway in Early Fall
photo.credit: NPS Photo 【4†Image: View of the Double Arch Bridge from Birdsong Hollow】 The elegant Double Arch Bridge won the Presidential Award for Design Excellence in 1995. It spans Birdsong Hollow and Tennessee Highway 96. To see it from below, take the TN 96 exit and stop at the pulloff before you get to the highway.

gwmp.description: Follow the Potomac corridor through woodland, waterfront views, and sites tied to American history. This scenic parkway links places to walk and pause within the busy Washington metropolitan area.

photo.alt: Stone Bridge Along the George Washington Memorial Parkway

jodr.description: Travel the forested corridor between Grand Teton and Yellowstone, following the upper Snake River through mountain country. The parkway honors John D. Rockefeller Jr.'s contributions to the national parks.

photo.alt: Granite mountains with a cloudy blue sky and green and yellow trees and plants in the foreground

abli.description: Visit the Kentucky birthplace landscape of Abraham Lincoln, where a formal memorial shelters a symbolic frontier cabin. The site connects his modest beginnings with the life that would lead him to the presidency.

photo.alt: The first memorial erected to honor Abraham Lincoln

adam.description: Explore the homes and gardens that held generations of the Adams family. From modest birthplaces to Peace field, the park brings the work of presidents, writers, and politically influential women into a domestic setting.

photo.alt: The Birthplaces of Presidents John Adams (right) and John Quincy Adams (left)

apco.description: Walk the village where Robert E. Lee surrendered the Army of Northern Virginia on April 9, 1865. The McLean House and surrounding landscape open the story of the war's end, emancipation, and the challenges of reunion.

photo.alt: A brick two story home with white pillars and railings.

bost.description: Follow Boston's revolutionary story through meeting places, monuments, and the historic harbor. These connected sites make the struggle for independence part of a walk through the living city.

photo.alt: A desk with paper and two sets of quills frame a person in colonial wear standing in the aisle.

cari.description: Explore the buildings and landscapes of Oakland and Magnolia plantations along Cane River. More than two centuries of Creole history emerge through the lives of enslaved workers, tenant families, and owners.

photo.alt: A small cabin sits beneath the branches of a Live Oak in the Oakland Plantation Quarters.

cebe.description: Read the Shenandoah Valley's history across farmland, Belle Grove, and the Cedar Creek battlefield. This fertile landscape connects generations of settlement and agriculture with a decisive Union victory in 1864.

photo.alt: American flag bunting hangs from the porch on a limestone building with a white portico.

chcu.description: Walk among monumental great houses in a broad desert canyon that flourished as an ancestral Pueblo center from 850 to 1250 CE. The scale of the masonry and surrounding landscape reveals a place that remains sacred to Indigenous communities.

photo.alt: Fajada Butte's silhoutte shown under a timelapse image of stars appearing in a vibrant circle above.

choh.description: Follow a canal-side pathway beside old locks, stone structures, and the Potomac River. The waterway carried coal, lumber, and farm goods for nearly a century, leaving a corridor where transportation history meets river scenery.

photo.alt: A gravel travel next to a watered canal surrounded by bright greenery

colo.description: Explore the landscapes of Jamestown and Yorktown, from the founding of the English settlement in 1607 to the Revolutionary victory of 1781. These places connect Virginia Indian, African, and European histories across the colonial era.

photo.alt: Wooden split rail fencing and flowering trees surround a grassy field behind an interpretive panel

cuga.description: Follow the mountain passage used by bison, Indigenous peoples, and later settlers crossing the Appalachians. Eighty-five miles of trails and 14,000 acres of wilderness reveal the ridges and valleys surrounding the historic gap.

photo.alt: Hensley Settlement

daav.description: Explore the Dayton places connected with Wilbur and Orville Wright and poet Paul Laurence Dunbar. Workshops, homes, and aviation landscapes bring their different paths of invention and expression into view.

photo.alt: A three-story brick building with tall green windows and a tall photo mural on the glass wall

frst.description: Explore Delaware's early story through historic places spread across the state and neighboring Pennsylvania. The park connects colonial rivalry, religious diversity, and the decision to become the first state to ratify the Constitution.

photo.alt: Red, yellow, and green leaves lay on the grass in front of a colonial building.

fosu.description: Look across Charleston Harbor from forts that witnessed both the Revolution and the opening of the Civil War. Fort Moultrie's 1776 defense and the attack on Fort Sumter in April 1861 frame two turning points in American history.

photo.alt: A row of cannon with Fort Moultrie in the background. A US flag is flying in the fort.

gero.description: Stand beside the Wabash River where George Rogers Clark's forces captured Fort Sackville in February 1779. The imposing memorial recalls a winter march through floodwaters and the Revolutionary struggle for the western frontier.

photo.alt: Fireworks over the Clark memorial

gosp.description: Stand where the transcontinental railroad joined in 1869, with open country stretching beyond the rails. Original railroad grades, construction traces, and replica steam locomotives bring the engineering achievement and its human labor into focus.

photo.alt: Two replica victorian age steam locomotives face each other on the original railroad grade

hafe.description: Walk a historic town tucked between the Potomac, Shenandoah, and steep Blue Ridge slopes. John Brown's raid, Civil War events, and Storer College's work in education and civil rights give its streets a remarkable depth of history.

photo.alt: View of Lower Town Harpers Ferry as seen from Maryland Heights

hart.description: Explore the community where Harriet Tubman made her home after moving to central New York in 1859. The park connects her later life with continuing work for family, freedom, faith, and human dignity.

photo.alt: A tall, green and orange painted church steeple, against a blue sky, with a tree in the foreground.

hatu.description: Explore Eastern Shore landscapes tied to Harriet Tubman's life and the journeys she led out of slavery. Marshes, fields, and waterways help make the risks and geography of the Underground Railroad tangible.

photo.alt: Girl stands on a bridge overlooking the marshlands.

home.description: Walk prairie and historic homestead ground while exploring the far-reaching Homestead Act of 1862. The park examines the opportunities settlers pursued and the profound changes imposed on Indigenous homelands.

photo.alt: A historic cabin stands next to a concrete path that leads to a plow shaped visitor center

hocu.description: Walk beside monumental earthworks created by Native American communities nearly 2,000 years ago. Mounds and geometric enclosures reveal ceremonial landscapes connected to gatherings, exchange, and religious life across a vast region.

photo.alt: An early morning sun casting long shadows over grass-covered mounds.

inde.description: Stand among the buildings and symbols at the heart of the nation's founding, including Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. The streets around them bring the debates over independence, government, and freedom into a compact historic landscape.

photo.alt: Color photo of Independence Hall as seen from the north side of Chestnut Street.

jela.description: Follow Louisiana's stories from bayou wetlands and alligator habitat to Cajun culture and the 1815 Battle of New Orleans. The park's separate sites connect living traditions with the landscapes and events that shaped the region.

photo.alt: Spanish moss hangs from live oak tree

jica.description: Explore the small Georgia town and rural setting that shaped Jimmy Carter. School, farm, and community stories trace the roots of the thirty-ninth president's life and public service.

photo.alt: A picture of the front of the home Jimmy Carter lived in as a young boy.

kewe.description: Explore the Keweenaw Peninsula's copper story through historic industrial communities and preserved places. Indigenous metalworking, nineteenth-century mining, and immigrant labor left traces across this Lake Superior landscape.

photo.alt: Two story stone and brick building. The American flag flies in front of a blue sky background

lewi.description: Explore coastal forests and Columbia River places linked with Lewis and Clark's expedition. The park connects the explorers' experience with the deeper and continuing history of the region's Native peoples.

photo.alt: A fifty foot square wooden fort surrounded by tall trees in a forest.

lowe.description: Follow canals and brick textile mills through a city transformed by waterpower. The park tells the industrial revolution through the work and lives of women factory workers and immigrant families.

photo.alt: 5 story brick factories with a clocktower surrounding a central courtyard

lyjo.description: Explore the Texas Hill Country places that shaped Lyndon B. Johnson, from his early community to the LBJ Ranch. The landscape connects family history, political life, and the president's final resting place.

photo.alt: President and Mrs. Johnson stand with their small, white dog in front of the Texas White House.
photo.credit: LBJ Library Photo by Frank Wolfe

mapr.description: Explore the places where secret wartime communities developed the first atomic bombs. Sites in Los Alamos, Hanford, and Oak Ridge connect scientific innovation with the lasting human consequences of the nuclear age.

photo.alt: Several women sit on stools along a long hallway full of dials and meters.

mabi.description: Walk the shaded paths of Mount Tom Forest through a landscape shaped by generations of conservation work. The estate connects managed woodland, restoration, and the people who helped change American ideas about stewardship.

photo.alt: scenic overlook with town below surrounded by fall foliage

malu.description: Walk the Atlanta neighborhood where Martin Luther King Jr. was born and grew up. His childhood home, church, and surrounding community connect everyday life under segregation with the roots of the civil rights movement.

photo.alt: Visitor center and the "I Have a Dream" Internrational World Peace Rose

mima.description: Follow the roads, fields, and historic structures tied to the fighting of April 19, 1775. The landscape between Lexington and Concord brings the opening of the American Revolution into walking distance.

photo.alt: The state of the Minute man stands atop a stone base. The wooden North Bridge is seen in the distanc

morr.description: Explore the places where Washington and the Continental Army endured the winter of 1779–1780. Encampment ground and historic buildings reveal the work of sustaining an army through severe cold and scarcity.

photo.alt: The Wick House surrounded by colorful fall leaves

natc.description: Explore historic places in a Mississippi River city shaped by cotton wealth, slavery, and the struggle for civil rights. The park brings different lives into the story of Natchez and the lower river.

photo.alt: Two story brick mansion with columns
photo.credit: NPS Photo 【4†Image: Two story brick townhouse】 The William Johnson House provides a window into the life of a free man of color whose published diary and personal papers provide a detailed account of daily life in the antebellum south.

nebe.description: Walk the historic waterfront district of a city built around the whaling trade. Streets and preserved buildings connect ocean voyages with the fortunes, labor, and communities that grew around them.

photo.alt: New Bedford Whaling National Historical Park Visitor Center on a bright fall day.

jazz.description: Explore the roots of jazz in the French Quarter through music, exhibits, and ranger programs. The park connects a sound heard around the world with the New Orleans communities that helped create it.

photo.alt: A young brass band musician plays a trumpet

nepe.description: Discover 38 places important to the history and culture of the nimíipuu, or Nez Perce, across four states. Valleys, prairies, and mountain landscapes reveal a homeland with a continuing cultural story.

photo.alt: Colorful painted tipi on green lawn

ocmu.description: Walk among great earthen mounds above the Ocmulgee River, built by Mississippian communities beginning around 900 CE. The park preserves evidence of thousands of years of Indigenous life in this landscape.

photo.alt: mounds

paal.description: Walk the prairie where U.S. and Mexican troops fought on May 8, 1846. The battlefield introduces the opening clash of a war that redrew North America's map and left a lasting borderland legacy.

photo.alt: Sunset over the battlefield

pagr.description: Watch the Passaic River plunge through the Great Falls in the heart of an industrial city. Founded as a planned manufacturing center in 1792, Paterson used this waterpower to drive mills and factories that reshaped American life.

photo.alt: Wind blows US Flag and surrounding area

peco.description: Explore a high-country crossroads where Pueblo communities, missionaries, traders, soldiers, and ranchers left their marks. The landscape opens a long story of movement, cultural encounter, and enduring traditions.

photo.alt: Large brown adobe mission church with low brick walls and kiva ladder in front

reer.description: Explore Beaufort County places where formerly enslaved people built new lives during Reconstruction. The park connects education, citizenship, work, and political change with the communities that helped define freedom after emancipation.

photo.alt: A two story brick building flanked by large live oak trees

rori.description: Explore Richmond's World War II home-front story through waterfront places and civilian experiences. The park follows the workers and families whose wartime opportunities, sacrifices, and unequal treatment changed their communities.

photo.alt: Entrance sign against the historic Ford buidling.

saga.description: Explore Augustus Saint-Gaudens's home, studio, and sculpture-filled landscape. Bronze works set among gardens and woodland connect an artist's creative process with the setting that inspired him.

photo.alt: sculpture of Abraham Lincoln

saan.description: Follow a chain of mission communities whose stone churches and grounds preserve layers of eighteenth-century history. These living places reveal Indigenous and Spanish encounters, cultural change, and the use of water and land along the San Antonio River.

photo.alt: White frescoed church with a stone ruin to the left in the foreground.

safr.description: Explore 50 acres around Aquatic Park Cove, where historic waterfront landmarks evoke San Francisco's seafaring past. Bay views and maritime stories connect the city with Pacific trade and life at sea.

photo.alt: Five historic ships docked at Mare Island

sajh.description: Explore saltwater shores, quiet woods, and native prairie at the island's former military camps. In 1859, a dispute sparked by the killing of a pig brought the United States and Britain close to war here.

photo.alt: a sun setting behind historic parade grounds

sara.description: Follow the fields and ridges where the 1777 Saratoga campaign ended in a British army's surrender. The landscape reveals a Revolutionary turning point with consequences far beyond the Hudson Valley.

photo.alt: A man wearing 18th-century clothing carrying a musket and a farmhouse are silhouetted by sunrise.

stge.description: Explore a Missouri river town established by French Canadian settlers by 1750. Distinctive historic houses and the town's agricultural story reveal a French colonial world along the Mississippi.

photo.alt: Frame house made of wood with U.S. and French flags flying on front porch.

edis.description: Step into the world of Thomas Edison's home and laboratory, where belt-driven machinery and experimental work helped shape modern life. The brick industrial complex makes invention feel like a working process.

photo.alt: Large salmon colored Victorian mansion with green lawn and blue sky

tuma.description: Explore the mission landscape of the Santa Cruz Valley, where O'odham, Yaqui, and Apache people encountered European missionaries and settlers. Timeworn paths and surviving structures reveal both conflict and cooperation at this cultural crossroads.

photo.alt: panorama of mission church with green grass and clouds

vafo.description: Explore 3,500 acres of meadows, woods, and historic ground where Washington's army camped in the winter of 1777–1778. The landscape connects the hardships of the encampment with the training and resolve that sustained the Revolution.

photo.alt: bronze statue of rev war general on stone base, red white and blue bunting behind

wefa.description: Explore more than 60 acres of woods, fields, and waterways around painter J. Alden Weir's home and studio. Paths through the farm reveal the scenes that inspired generations of American artists.

photo.alt: A view of the south side of the Weir House with porch visable, showing a fence in front of the home

wori.description: Explore the places tied to the 1848 Women's Rights Convention in Seneca Falls. The park connects the gathering's demands with the people and reform movements that carried the struggle for equality forward.

photo.alt: The Wesleyan Chapel in summer

asis.description: Walk from Atlantic beaches into salt marshes, coastal bays, and maritime forest on a shifting barrier island. Assateague's wild horses are part of a landscape continually reshaped by wind and waves.

photo.alt: Wild horses on the dunes at Assateague

cana.description: Explore dunes, coastal hammocks, and the waters of Mosquito Lagoon along a protected barrier island. Timucua shell mounds reveal a human story reaching thousands of years into this coastal landscape.

photo.alt: Dune plants, beach, and ocean.

caco.description: Explore 40 miles of Outer Cape beach, with dunes, marshes, ponds, and woodland beyond the surf. Lighthouses and wild cranberry bogs connect the shore's scenery with Cape Cod's continuing ways of life.

photo.alt: A curling wave breaks against the backdrop of a pink sunrise.

caha.description: Follow a chain of barrier islands where ocean beaches give way to quiet salt marshes and sounds. Lighthouse landscapes and paddling waters reveal a coast continually changed by wind, water, and storms.

photo.alt: A beach landscape with the black and white spiraled lighthouse in the background

calo.description: Cross by boat to barrier islands with wide beaches, historic villages, and the diamond-patterned Cape Lookout Lighthouse. Remote shores and horse habitat on Shackleford Banks give this seashore a distinctly offshore character.

photo.alt: : Black & white patterned tower of the Cape Lookout Lighthouse stands against a blue & white cloud f
photo.credit: NPS photo 【4†Image: A bird with orange bill and orange legs runs along the tide line. Waves in the background】 The American Oystercatcher, one of the protected species in the park, forages along the shoreline.

cuis.description: Leave the mainland for maritime forest, broad marshes, and undeveloped Atlantic beaches. More than 9,800 acres of designated wilderness sit within an island landscape layered with Indigenous, African American, and industrial-era history.

photo.alt: Sand dunes covered with shrubs and grasses

fiis.description: Explore a barrier island of high dunes, Atlantic beaches, and old maritime forest. Lighthouse scenery and historic places add depth to a coastal landscape just beyond the pressure of New York City.

photo.alt: A wide shot of the white and black striped Fire Island Lighthouse from the beach.

guis.description: Explore white-sand barrier islands, marshes, and clear coastal waters across Florida and Mississippi. Historic forts add another layer to beaches reached by both road and boat.

photo.alt: A fort with water on an island
photo.credit: NPS/Bernstiel 【4†Image: White sand and green water】 The Santa Rosa Area is the stech of beach between Navarre and Pensacola Beach. There is a fee area called Opal Beach.

pais.description: Explore 66 miles of protected coastline, where Gulf beaches meet coastal prairie and the hypersaline Laguna Madre. Dunes and tidal flats reveal a barrier-island landscape shaped by water, wind, and a long human history.

photo.alt: Yellow flowers bloom in the dunes along Malaquite Beach.

pore.description: Follow forested ridges and open grasslands toward rocky headlands and broad Pacific beaches. More than 1,500 plant and animal species share a peninsula whose lighthouse and cultural places add human stories to the scenery.

photo.alt: A long concrete staircase down to a red roofed, white lighthouse on cliffs above the ocean.

afbg.description: Pause at the Manhattan burial ground of free and enslaved Africans whose work helped build early New York. The memorial and exhibits restore individual lives and a long-obscured community to the city's history.

photo.alt: African Burial Ground Memorial

agfo.description: Explore prairie hills where paleontologists uncovered complete skeletons of extinct Miocene mammals in the early twentieth century. Exhibits also connect the landscape with Lakota history and the friendship between James Cook and Chief Red Cloud.

photo.alt: The visitor center sits in the middle of mixed grass prairie.

alfl.description: Explore the source of colorful flint used by people of the High Plains for some 13,000 years. The quarries connect a striking stone with toolmaking, trade, and survival across generations.

photo.alt: Turtle Petroglyph at Antelope Creek Village Site
photo.credit: NPS Photo 【4†Image: A view of the gardens and Alibates Visitor Center.】 The gardens and Alibates Visitor Center host activities and ranger-led programs throughout the year.

azru.description: Walk through an ancestral Pueblo great house with original wooden beams and intricate stonework. A restored Great Kiva helps reveal the scale and communal life of this sacred Chacoan place.

photo.alt: Reconstructed stone kiva amidst stone ruins

band.description: Explore more than 33,000 acres of canyons and mesas, where homes carved into soft cliffs stand beside masonry walls and petroglyphs. These ancestral Pueblo places connect the landscape with cultures that continue in surrounding communities.

photo.alt: the village of Tyuonyi

bepa.description: Step into the historic headquarters where the National Woman's Party organized for women's equality. Close to the Capitol, the house connects Alice Paul's campaigns with the long struggle for the Equal Rights Amendment.

photo.alt: Belmont-Paul Women's Equality NM House

bicr.description: Explore places tied to Birmingham's pivotal 1963 civil rights campaign. The district reveals the courage of nonviolent protesters and the brutal response that brought segregation's injustice before a worldwide audience.

photo.alt: 4 separate statues of the four little girls who were killed in the 16th st Baptist Church bombing

bowa.description: Explore the Virginia farm where Booker T. Washington was born into slavery in 1856. The landscape introduces the early life of the educator who later led Tuskegee and became an influential author and public figure.

photo.alt: Tobacco field being plowed by man with two draft horses

cabr.description: Look over San Diego Bay from Point Loma while exploring the story of Cabrillo's 1542 expedition. Coastal trails and historic features connect Pacific scenery with centuries of human use.

photo.alt: Tidepools at Cabrillo

cane.description: Walk the ground of a Civil War supply depot that became a major recruiting and training center for United States Colored Troops. Camp Nelson also sheltered families and people escaping slavery in pursuit of freedom.

photo.alt: A paved path leads to a gray wooden building with US Flag flying.

cach.description: Look into deep sandstone canyons where ancient homes and images share the landscape with living Diné communities. Navajo families continue to farm, raise livestock, and maintain connections reaching across many generations.

photo.alt: Farm in the canyon

cavo.description: Walk a volcanic rim above northeastern New Mexico's plains, within the 8,000-square-mile Raton-Clayton Volcanic Field. The cinder cone offers a vivid introduction to the eruptions that shaped this broad landscape.

photo.alt: A cloud shrouded volcano rises behind a field of yellow flowers.

cagr.description: Stand beside the Great House, a remarkable earthen structure left by an Ancestral Sonoran Desert farming community. The site reveals a world of irrigation canals, trade, and interconnected desert settlements.

photo.alt: eathern building under modern roof structure

casa.description: Explore the Spanish stone fortress built to defend St. Augustine and Atlantic trade routes. Its walls frame the waterfront while revealing centuries of conflict and cultural encounter in Florida.

photo.alt: Drawbridge entrance to the Castillo de San Marcos

cacl.description: Step inside a harbor fort at Manhattan's southern tip that later served theatergoers and arriving immigrants. Castle Clinton's changing uses trace New York's growth from a defended port into a gateway city.

photo.alt: Castle Clinton NM Entrance

camo.description: Explore nearly 21,000 acres of Mojave Desert grasslands, Joshua tree forests, and rugged mountain scenery. This remote landscape beside Mojave National Preserve also holds traces of a rich human past.

photo.alt: Red rocks frame a stand of Joshua trees and sage brush.

cebr.description: Look into a half-mile-deep amphitheater of eroded rock from a rim above 10,000 feet. Bristlecone pines, subalpine forest, and high meadows surround the dramatic basin.

photo.alt: The ground falls away from the viewer creating brilliant rock formations of pink, red, and orange.

cech.description: Explore the place associated with Cesar Chavez's leadership of the farmworker movement. The monument connects organizing for better wages and safer conditions with the people who built a lasting agricultural union.

photo.alt: A walkway with a fountain

chyo.description: Explore the life of Charles Young, a military leader who advanced through the ranks despite entrenched racism. His Ohio home connects personal achievement with the wider history of the Buffalo Soldiers and the fight for equality.

photo.alt: A large grey house with dark grey shutters with a green lawn out front under a blue sky

colm.description: Follow Rim Rock Drive above sheer red-rock canyons and towering monoliths. Overlooks and trails reveal a plateau landscape that also provides habitat for bighorn sheep and eagles.

photo.alt: sandstone spire hundreds of feet tall stands above sparsely vegetated canyon bottom and cliffs

crmo.description: Explore dark lava flows, cinder cones, and islands of sagebrush across a stark volcanic landscape. Trails through the monument reveal the textures and forms left by successive eruptions.

photo.alt: A close-up shot of a folded, waving sea of lava rock, with mountains in the far distance.

depo.description: Stand below basalt columns rising as much as 60 feet, then follow mountain trails toward 101-foot Rainbow Falls. Protected since 1911, the monument pairs unusual volcanic geometry with Sierra scenery.

photo.alt: The Devils Postpile basalt formation resembles tall columns.

deto.description: Follow the base of a huge, fluted rock tower rising above the prairie near the Black Hills. The formation is sacred to many Northern Plains Indigenous peoples and holds cultural meaning beyond its striking geology.

photo.alt: Devils Tower looming above the trees

dino.description: See dinosaur fossils still embedded in the rock, then explore desert canyons cut by winding rivers. Petroglyphs and historic places add human stories to a landscape whose fossil record reaches back about 150 million years.

photo.alt: the fossilized skull of camarasaurus dinosaur

efmo.description: Walk wooded Mississippi River bluffs among more than 200 Indigenous mounds. These sacred earthworks invite careful reflection on the communities that built them and the Tribal nations whose connections continue.

photo.alt: Bear Effigy Mounds with visitor walking nearby.

elma.description: Explore lava flows, cinder cones, sandstone bluffs, and the rough textures of a volcanic landscape. Generations of people have found ways to live and travel through this apparently forbidding terrain.

photo.alt: Yellow sandstone cliff at sunset with dark lava field in background

elmo.description: Follow a sandstone bluff to the waterhole that drew travelers here for centuries. More than 2,000 petroglyphs, names, dates, and messages connect ancestral Pueblo, Spanish, and American journeys.

photo.alt: El Morro with Sunflowers

flfo.description: Explore a mountain valley where petrified redwood stumps reach up to 14 feet across. Delicate insect and plant fossils reveal a prehistoric Colorado very different from today's grassy landscape.

photo.alt: Fossil redwood stump
photo.credit: NPS Photo 【4†Image: palaeovespa, ancient wasp】 Captured 34 million years ago, this ancient wasp and other insects are on display at Florissant Fossil Beds NM.

fofr.description: Walk the traces of a British colonial town and fort established by James Oglethorpe in 1736. Archaeology brings the lives of its residents into the story of Britain and Spain's struggle over the southern frontier.

photo.alt: Ruin of Soldier Barracks at Fort Frederica NM

foma.description: See a coquina watchtower completed in 1742 to guard St. Augustine's southern approach. Around it, roughly 300 protected acres preserve a coastal mosaic of dunes, marsh, and maritime forest.

photo.alt: Fort Matanzas, a fortified watch tower made form coquina.

fomc.description: Walk the harbor defenses whose survival during the September 1814 Battle of Baltimore inspired the words of the national anthem. The star-shaped fort also holds stories from the Civil War through World War II.

photo.alt: A large American flag waved over the brick sallyport of an old fort.

fomr.description: Explore the coastal fort where people escaping slavery sought freedom during the Civil War. Old Point Comfort's longer history links Indigenous homelands, the 1619 arrival of enslaved Africans, and centuries of national defense.

photo.alt: Aerial View of Fort Monroe

fopu.description: Explore the brick fortress where rifled artillery demonstrated the vulnerability of masonry defenses during the Civil War. Massive walls and the surrounding coastal landscape make a turning point in military technology tangible.

photo.alt: The red masonry walls of Fort Pulaski still show battle damage over 150 years later.

fost.description: Explore a fort associated with the struggle to control the Oneida Carrying Place, the vital portage linking eastern waterways with the Great Lakes. The site connects military rivalry with the homelands and choices of the Six Nations Confederacy.

photo.alt: A cannon crew fires towards a wooden fort. An explosion of fire jets out in front of them.

foun.description: Walk among adobe walls rising from shortgrass prairie beside traces of the Santa Fe Trail. From 1851 to 1891, Fort Union helped reshape life, trade, and military power across the Southwest.

photo.alt: Panorama of Officers Row
photo.credit: Ron Harvey - Fort Union National Monument

fobu.description: Explore fossil-rich ridges that preserve an ancient freshwater lake and its surrounding life. Exceptionally detailed fish, plants, and other animals reveal a warm, wet world beneath today's Wyoming landscape.

photo.alt: A dark brown, football-shaped fossil fish with a fan-shaped tail and spines standing up on its back.

frri.description: Explore the story of the Freedom Riders, whose 1961 challenge to segregated interstate travel met violent resistance in Alabama. The monument connects the attack near Anniston with a campaign that changed the civil rights struggle.

photo.alt: Colored Greyhound mural with historical information about the Freedom Riders

gewa.description: Explore 551 acres in Virginia's Northern Neck where George Washington was born in 1732. The family landscape also reveals how later generations chose to remember his beginnings.

photo.alt: Two buildings surrounded by green foliage with a brick path leading to the buildings.

gwca.description: Walk the farm landscape that helped awaken George Washington Carver's curiosity about plants. The monument connects his childhood with the scientist, educator, and humanitarian he became.

photo.alt: Bronze status of young George Washington Carver atop a large boulder, on the Carver trail.

gicl.description: Follow a canyon trail to rooms built inside natural caves by Mogollon people in the late 1200s. The surviving walls make family life and skilled construction tangible within a rugged mountain setting.

photo.alt: Sunrise view of Gila Cliff Dwellings with brilliant sky.

gois.description: Cross New York Harbor to an island shaped by nearly two centuries of Army and Coast Guard service. Historic fortifications place the city's waterfront in a wider story of defense and national service.

photo.alt: Bridge over dry moat leading into a gated fort.

grpo.description: Explore a reconstructed fur-trade depot on Lake Superior and the pathways that linked it with inland waters. The monument tells the partnership between the Grand Portage Anishinaabe and the North West Company, with continuing Tribal stewardship today.

photo.alt: Three log buildings with Lake and point of land in background.

hafo.description: Discover fossils of horses, mastodons, ground sloths, and other animals from a very different Idaho. The monument reveals the wetlands, forests, and grasslands that supported life during the Pliocene.

photo.alt: A fossil horse stands in the center of a room filled with posters and display cases

pima.description: This protected archaeological place preserves the story of an ancestral Sonoran Desert community and its farming landscape. It lies on Gila River Indian Community land and is not open for public visitation.

hove.description: Follow canyon rims to multistory stone towers balanced on ledges and boulders. Built between 1200 and 1300 CE, Hovenweep's six settlement groups preserve a striking ancestral Pueblo landscape.

photo.alt: Tall stone structures with a setting sun shining through them. Desert landscape surrounds them.

jeca.description: Explore a small portion of an underground system with more than 220 surveyed miles of passage. Guided cave routes reveal delicate formations and the intricate spaces hidden beneath the Black Hills.

photo.alt: The target room inside Jewel Cave.

joda.description: Explore a fossil landscape that records changing climates, forests, and grasslands across ancient Oregon. Exhibits and colorful rock formations reveal worlds inhabited by early horses, brontotheres, and other long-vanished mammals.

photo.alt: Painted Hills

kaww.description: Explore wooded country threaded by rivers and streams, with broad views toward Katahdin. Trails and water routes connect Maine's northern landscape with a human history reaching back millennia.

photo.alt: A blue night sky filled with stars sits over reflective water. Dark trees line the image.

labe.description: Explore a volcanic landscape shaped by the Medicine Lake volcano, with more than 800 caves and rugged high-desert terrain. Rock art, campsites, and battlefields connect its geology with Indigenous history and conflict.

photo.alt: Sunrise at Lava Beds

libi.description: Walk the hills where Lakota, Cheyenne, and Arapaho warriors fought the U.S. Seventh Cavalry on June 25–26, 1876. Memorials and battlefield places invite reflection on the battle and the policies that threatened Indigenous ways of life.

photo.alt: The sun sets behind the Indian Memorial.

memy.description: Encounter the family home of civil rights organizers Medgar and Myrlie Evers. Medgar's assassination here in June 1963 connects this modest house with a national struggle for equality and justice.

photo.alt: A small ranch-style home, aqua in color with light brown brick accents, sits on a shaded lot.

misp.description: Explore rolling Kentucky fields where Union forces won an important early Civil War victory. The battlefield reveals why control of this border state mattered to both sides.

photo.alt: A orange sunset over the white granite headstones in the national cemetery with silhouetted cannon.

moca.description: Look up at a twenty-room dwelling tucked into a limestone cliff above the desert. Protected since 1906, this remarkable structure reveals the ingenuity of the people who made a home here.

photo.alt: A 5-story masonry dwelling sits in a cliff alcove.

muwo.description: Walk beneath old-growth coast redwoods along Redwood Creek, where fog and flowing water sustain the forest. Protected since 1908, the grove offers an intimate encounter with towering trees close to San Francisco.

photo.alt: beams of light from the top left corner of the image beam into a forest of towering redwood trunks

nabr.description: Look down on three great sandstone bridges or follow trails into the canyons beneath them. Protected since 1908, these spans reveal the power of flowing water in a dry ancestral Pueblo landscape.

photo.alt: A large sandstone natural bridge with surrounding canyons and vegetation

nava.description: Look across sandstone canyons toward ancestral homes sheltered in natural alcoves. The villages were last occupied around 1300, but remain spiritually important to the Hopi, Zuni, Paiute, and Navajo peoples connected with this place.

photo.alt: view from inside the Betatakin Cliff Dwelling looking out.

orca.description: Enter twisting passages carved by acidic water through marble in the Siskiyou Mountains. Guided cave routes reveal an underground landscape, while forest trails explore the mountain above.

photo.alt: Miller's Chapel at Oregon Caves

orpi.description: Explore a living Sonoran Desert of distinctive cacti, mountain backdrops, and hidden animal habitats. Scenic drives and wilderness paths connect this biosphere reserve with thousands of years of desert life.

photo.alt: Organ pipe cactus and mountains at sunset

petr.description: Follow volcanic rock escarpments marked with designs carved by Native Americans and Spanish settlers some 400 to 700 years ago. These images remain culturally and spiritually important to their descendants.

photo.alt: Petroglyphs on dark boulders with a cloudy sky.

pisp.description: Explore a spring-centered landscape where Kaibab Paiute traditions meet the history of Mormon settlement. A fort, cabins, and gardens reveal why this water source mattered in the arid country.

photo.alt: A glittering sky of stars glows above a historic covered wagon.

pipe.description: Follow the red-stone landscape where Indigenous people have quarried pipestone for more than 3,000 years. The continuing creation of ceremonial pipes makes this a living sacred place.

photo.alt: Purple and yellow wildflowers in a field of tall grass
photo.credit: NPS Photo 【4†Image: Pink wall of rock next to path and grass】 The outcroppings along the trail are a surprise to many visitors expecting a flat prairie

popo.description: Walk among monumental earthworks built by a sophisticated culture some 3,000 years ago. Poverty Point's scale and far-reaching trade connections reveal an extraordinary ancient center in the lower Mississippi region.

photo.alt: A grassy green mound.

pull.description: Walk a planned industrial neighborhood known for its distinctive architecture and urban design. Pullman's preserved places reveal how race, gender, labor, and economic power shaped the opportunities of people who lived and worked here.

photo.alt: The Pullman National Historical Park Visitor Center

rabr.description: Approach a vast natural sandstone bridge tucked within remote canyon country. Rainbow Bridge is sacred to neighboring Tribal nations, giving this remarkable span a significance beyond its geology.

photo.alt: A large natural rock arch spans a canyon with people looking up at it.

ruca.description: Explore the story of a rock shelter used by people for about 12,000 years. Although the cave itself is closed to entry, the archaeological record reveals changing technologies and lifeways across the prehistoric Southeast.

photo.alt: Russell Cave in Spring

sapu.description: Explore three separate landscapes of Pueblo settlements and Spanish mission remains. Their walls reveal cultural exchange, conflict, and the difficult consequences of early colonial encounters in New Mexico.

photo.alt: Pink flowers and green foliage frame the roofless remains of a stone mission.

scbl.description: Look up at an 800-foot landmark above the North Platte River, recognized by Indigenous peoples and emigrant travelers alike. Across 3,000 acres, trails and overlooks connect sweeping prairie scenery with the Oregon, California, and Mormon trails.
